clue.text: Cook given a so-called award for pasta

parts.note: to cook the books is to rig them, so cook here means rig

indicators.note: so-called says the word for the award is only as spoken, with its spelling changed

parts.note: a Tony is the American theatre award

explanation.surface: A chef receives an award for a pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called' asks for the sound of TONY, written TONI. A Tony is the Broadway theatre prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged tubes of pasta are an example of the general food named.

clue.text: Articles about walls of Gulliver's city

indicators.note: about means going round, so the articles surround the other letters

parts.note: two indefinite articles, a and a

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Grammar articles concerning the fortifications of a city in Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city famous for the Taj Mahal is an example of a city.

clue.text: Tense little boy is difficult to handle

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
Ricky is a boy's pet name, a diminutive of Richard

explanation.surface: A nervous child proves hard to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation hard to handle is awkward or tricky, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One leaving latticework erected in sink

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means set upright, so the letters read from the bottom up
leaving means the numeral departs from the lattice word

parts.note: an espalier is a lattice on which fruit trees are trained
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a trellis put up over a sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I out of ESPALIER to leave ESPALER; 'erected' turns that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink back into illness or bad habits is to relapse, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Twilight of the Gods depicted in cloth over holy book

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth

indicators.note: over signals that the holy book's name is turned round

parts.note: the Koran is the holy book of Islam

explanation.surface: The end of the gods is pictured on fabric laid over a scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the final battle destroying the gods is known in German as Götterdämmerung, the Twilight of the Gods.

clue.text: Tea (and most of its value) produced for ducal mansion

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea

indicators.note: most of means one letter of the word its is dropped

parts.note: worth means value

explanation.surface: Tea and a large share of its worth were produced for a duke's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the I from ITS, leaving TS.
explanation.definitionFit: This Derbyshire stately home is the seat of the Dukes of Devonshire, an example of a ducal mansion.

clue.text: Note found by lake in a supernatural place

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A message is discovered beside a lake in an enchanted spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairyland, the realm of the fairies, is a magical place in old poetic spelling.

clue.text: Bring up blood containing tiny bit of gallstone after not finishing food

indicators.note: after places the shortened food word in front of the rest
not finishing means the food word loses its final letter

parts.note: a dish is an item of food

indicators.note: containing means the blood word holds the next letter inside

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: a tiny bit of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A patient coughs up blood with a fragment of gallstone after leaving food unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up food is to vomit it, a phrasal synonym for disgorge.

clue.text: England's fifth king stopping imposter's retreat

indicators.note: fifth asks for the fifth letter of the word England
stopping means plugging a gap, so the letter goes inside the imposter word

parts.note: a sham is an imposter or fraud
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: An English king holds up a pretender's place of withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu hermitage or religious retreat is called by this name.

clue.text: Wally's relative?

parts.note: a wally is a fool, and a ... is both a fool and a grandmother, so the word is a relative in two senses

explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for an idiot; nana is another. Read as a family member, a nana is a granny.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a silly person, and also a family word for grandmother.

clue.text: Saint prepared to fulfil task in shop

indicators.note: to fulfil here means to fill out, so the mixed letters fill the task word

parts.note: a chore is a task

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of saint are worked up anew

explanation.surface: A saint is ready to carry out a job in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges SAINT to AINST, which goes inside CHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A store belonging to a group of branches is a type of shop.

clue.text: Awkward lad capturing unfulfilled ladies' hearts

indicators.note: capturing means the boy word holds the other letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: unfulfilled means the word ladies is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A clumsy young man wins the affection of women who are left unsatisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang for uncooperative or difficult, a synonym of awkward.

clue.text: Limitless poteen found in apostles' pants and overalls

indicators.note: pants as a verb means gasps, read here as an untidy jumble, signalling rearrangement
limitless here keeps only the central pair of letters of poteen

explanation.surface: Irish moonshine is found in the trousers and overalls of the apostles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limitless' gives TE, the middle of POTEEN; 'pants' rearranges TE with APOSTLES. Poteen is Irish illicit whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Padded ski trousers with a bib top are a kind of overalls.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying crop is badly drawn

indicators.note: carrying means the vehicle word holds the other inside

parts.note: a sled is a vehicle for snow
the craw is the crop, a bird's food pouch

explanation.surface: A cart hauling a harvest is poorly sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop' looks like a harvest but is a bird's craw.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing or drawing done hastily and untidily is scrawled.

clue.text: Sack attendant nursing ailment

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the attendant word holds the ailment

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
an ill is an ailment

explanation.surface: A dismissed helper cares for an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Drinks to setter's game

parts.note: gin and rum are drinks
the setter's means belonging to me, my

explanation.surface: Here's to the crossword compiler's sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for two players is an example of a game.

clue.text: Margin containing recipe associated with English root vegetable

indicators.note: containing means the margin word holds the next letters

parts.note: a skirt is an edge or margin, as in the skirt of a wood
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin take

explanation.surface: A recipe in the margin is linked to an English root crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant of the parsley family grown for its sweet edible roots is a kind of vegetable.

clue.text: One German-American author was a genius

parts.note: ein is German for one
Gertrude Stein was an American author

explanation.surface: A German-American writer was brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German-American' reads as one description but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's surname is used to mean any brilliant person.

clue.text: Leader of Georgian separatists means to escape

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group
a way is a means

explanation.surface: The head of a Georgian breakaway group plans a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: To get away is to flee, so the phrasal verb matches escape.

clue.text: Dish out pies cooked by daughter new to the Home Counties

indicators.note: cooked means made up, so the pies letters are reworked

parts.note: SE, the southeast, is where the Home Counties around London lie

explanation.surface: A daughter newly arrived near London serves up the pies she baked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges PIES to ISPE. The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish out food is to hand it out, the same as dispense.

clue.text: Nice mansion, home to comic superhero

indicators.note: home to says the phrase houses the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A pleasant big house is where a comic-book hero lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A frost-powered X-Men member is an example of a comic-book superhero.

clue.text: Angelica root included in runny centre of spicy sesame paste

indicators.note: included in means the letter goes inside the runny word

parts.note: thin means runny, of a liquid

indicators.note: a word's root is its first letter, where it starts
the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A herb's root goes into the runny middle of a spiced sesame spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spicy' looks like it describes the paste, but only its centre letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: This Middle Eastern paste is ground from sesame seeds.

clue.text: Rope carried by private therapist

indicators.note: carried by says the letters are held within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A rope is brought by a counsellor in private practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or chain used to tie an animal.

clue.text: Research by American leaving sign for social worker in place to eat

parts.note: res is short for research

indicators.note: leaving means the American letters depart from the sign

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: Research by an American lacking a social worker's credentials leads to a diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a job but is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant is somewhere to have a meal.

clue.text: End of barrel?

definitions.meaning: the end of a cigarette or a rifle stock
a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the thick end of a thing and a large wine cask.

clue.text: Unforeseen hitch involving lid of brown sauce

indicators.note: the lid of a word is its top, the first letter in a down clue

parts.note: lip, like sauce, means cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: An unexpected snag involving the top of a bottle of brown sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' is cheek, LIP. Brown sauce is a British table condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is a brief, unexpected problem or setback.

clue.text: Fish served with starters of egg mayonnaise for doctor

parts.note: hake is a fish

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: Fish is served with egg mayonnaise starters for the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like menu courses but means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Muslim countries a physician, especially a traditional healer, is called by this title.

clue.text: A saint leaving tipsy priest provided with drink

indicators.note: leaving means the saint letter departs from the mixed letters
tipsy means drunk, so the priest letters are jumbled

parts.note: if means provided, as in on condition that

explanation.surface: A saint walks away from a drunken priest who has been given a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' rearranges PRIEST and 'leaving' removes S, giving PERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.
